rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The six trigonometric ratios come from a right triangle: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan θ = sin θ/cos θ, with cosec, sec and cot their reciprocals, and their special values at 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90° are tabulated. Three fundamental identities tie the ratios together: sin^2 θ + cos^2 θ = 1, 1 + tan^2 θ = sec^2 θ and 1 + cot^2 θ = cosec^2 θ.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: x sin(A+B) = sin A + sin B. x Must use compound angle formula.  ·  x tan 2A = 2 tan A. x tan 2A = 2tan A/(1-tan^2 A).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: sec 90° = 1/cos 90° and tan 90° = sin 90°/cos 90° are undefined because cos 90° = 0, and cosec 0° is undefined because sin 0° = 0.  ·  The double angle formulas are just the compound angle formulas with B = A, so a proof of one family gives the other.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Prove: sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1  ·  If sin theta = 3/5, find all other trig ratios.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: tan(A + B) needs 1 - tan A tan B != 0; when it is zero the sum is 90° (mod 180°) and the tangent is undefined even though sin and cos are well defined.  ·  The identity sin(A + B) sin(A - B) = sin^2 A - sin^2 B is a product-to-sum result often asked as a proof, with the right side reached by expanding both factors.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Given one trigonometric ratio and the quadrant of the angle, find all the other ratios by applying the relevant identity and the signs of that quadrant.  ·  Prove an identity by starting from one side and transforming it, line by line, into the other side using the fundamental identities.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: To get all the ratios from sin θ = 3/5, build the right triangle with hypotenuse 5, opposite 3 and adjacent 4, then read off cos = 4/5 and tan = 3/4.  ·  For cos 2A choose 2cos^2 A - 1 or 1 - 2sin^2 A, since using cos^2 A - sin^2 A forces you to find the other ratio first.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Prove that sin^2 θ + cos^2 θ = 1.  ·  If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, find cos θ, tan θ, sec θ, cosec θ and cot θ.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Finding the remaining ratios from one given ratio is the most common 2-mark question, and the quadrant must be stated.  ·  Proving an identity is a standard 5-mark question, with marks for starting from one side, for each valid step, and for reaching the other side.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Ratios in a right triangle: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan θ = opposite/adjacent = sin θ/cos θ.  ·  Reciprocal ratios: cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ and cot θ = 1/tan θ = cos θ/sin θ.  ·  The identity sin^2 θ + cos^2 θ = 1 and its two rearrangements 1 + tan^2 θ = sec^2 θ and 1 + cot^2 θ = cosec^2 θ.  ·  Compound angles: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B and cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B, where the two signs are always opposite for cosine.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: sin(A + B) is not sin A + sin B; the compound angle formula must be used instead.  ·  In the cosine formula the signs are opposite, so cos(A + B) = cos A cos B - sin A sin B while cos(A - B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B.  ·  cos 2A has three forms, and the useful one is the one matching what you are given: 2cos^2 A - 1 if you know cos A, or 1 - 2sin^2 A if you know sin A.  ·  tan 2A = 2 tan A/(1 - tan^2 A), not 2 tan A, and it is undefined when tan A = ±1.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Prove that sin(A + B) sin(A - B) = sin^2 A - sin^2 B.  ·  Solve 2sin^2 x - sin x - 1 = 0 for 0° <= x <= 360°.  ·  If cos A = 4/5 and sin B = 3/5 with A and B acute, find sin(A + B) and cos 2A.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Evaluating sin(A + B) or cos 2A from given ratios is a 5-mark question, and the answer is left as an exact fraction with a surd.  ·  MCQs give a value from the table of standard angles and ask for the ratio of another angle, or give an equation and ask for its solutions in a stated interval.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Double angles as the case B = A: sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A, cos 2A = cos^2 A - sin^2 A = 2cos^2 A - 1 = 1 - 2sin^2 A, and tan 2A = 2 tan A/(1 - tan^2 A).  ·  Standard values: sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = 1/sqrt(2), sin 60° = sqrt(3)/2, with cosine running in the reverse order and tan 45° = 1, tan 30° = 1/sqrt(3), tan 60° = sqrt(3).  ·  tan θ = sin θ/cos θ requires cos θ != 0, which is why tan 90° is undefined while sin 90° = 1 and cos 90° = 0.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Because the standard values are exact surds, exact answers should be left as fractions with surds rather than rounded decimals.  ·  In a right triangle sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan θ = opposite/adjacent, while cosec θ, sec θ and cot θ are the reciprocals of sin, cos and tan.  ·  The fundamental identities are sin^2 θ + cos^2 θ = 1, 1 + tan^2 θ = sec^2 θ and 1 + cot^2 θ = cosec^2 θ.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The compound angle formulas are sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B, cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B and tan(A ± B) = (tan A ± tan B)/(1 ∓ tan A tan B).  ·  The double angle formulas are sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A, cos 2A = cos^2 A - sin^2 A = 2cos^2 A - 1 = 1 - 2sin^2 A and tan 2A = 2 tan A/(1 - tan^2 A).  ·  If sin θ = 3/5 for an acute angle then cos θ = 4/5 and tan θ = 3/4, so a single known ratio and the quadrant determine all the others.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: When solving in 0° <= x <= 360°, remember that sin x = c and cos x = c give two angles each while tan x = c gives only one per period.  ·  Fix the signs from the quadrant, where sin is positive in I and II, cos in I and IV, and tan in I and III, which is faster than calculation.  ·  Prove: sin(A+B)sin(A-B) = sin^2 A - sin^2 B
